steps.text:
Materials Needed: Colored tiles, three each of five different colors.

Overview: This posttest checks if the student has mastered the 7 essential phonemic awareness skills. They should have at least 95% accuracy (maximum 1 error per task). If they miss 2 or more on any task, stop the test and return to the lowest lesson number circled on the answer sheet.

sections.title: Task A: Break Apart Nonsense Words

steps.text: Let's break a word into sounds. Some of these words have two sounds, but some of them have three. So you'll have to listen carefully. Ready? The first word is SNI.
Expected: SNI
Now say it again ... very slowly.
Expected: /ssss/-/nnnn/-/iiii/
How many sounds did you hear in that word?
Expected: 3
Good listening. Pull down the tiles.
Now touch-and-say each sound.
Student touches the first tile and says /s/, touches the second tile and says /n/, then touches the third tile and says /i/.
Now wash those tiles off.

Dictate the following words one by one. Score accuracy for breaking sounds apart:
1. NACH
2. OK
3. USP
4. PIP
5. GLA
6. OPT
7. THA
8. SHRO
9. TOB
10. IM
11. SKA
12. ILT
13. BO
14. TRI
15. SHAD
Now you'll break a word, then I'll change a sound. Some of these words have 2 sounds, others have 3. Ready? The first word is SKA.
Expected: SKA
Say it again ... very slowly.
Expected: /ssss/-/k/-/aaaa/
Pull down the tiles.
Touch-and-say.
Student touches first tile and says /s/, touches second tile and says /k/, touches third tile and says /a/.
Now watch carefully. I'm going to change this sound to /o/.
To figure out the new word, touch-and-say the sounds.
Student touches first tile and says /s/, touches second tile and says /k/, touches third tile and says /o/.
Slowly blend those sounds into a word.
Expected: /ssss/-/k/-/oooo/
Now say it fast like a word.
Expected: SKO
Now watch carefully. I'm going to take out this tile.
Touch-and-say the sounds that are left.
Student touches first tile and says /k/, touches second tile and says /o/.
Slowly blend.
Expected: /k/-/oooo/
Now say it fast like a word.
Expected: KO
Great. Go ahead and wash off those tiles.

Dictate the following sets for the student to break, replace, and remove:
1. VAK -> VOK -> VO
2. DA -> LA -> A
3. IMP -> ISP -> IP
4. UJ -> UK -> U
5. BLO -> BLI -> BI
Now we're going to compare two words. The first word is SPA.
Expected: SPA
Say it slowly.
Expected: /ssss/-/p/-/aaaa/
Touch-and-say using the first row.
Student touches first tile and says /s/, touches second tile and says /p/, touches the third tile and says /a/.
Good. The second word is SPI.
Expected: SPI
Slowly.
Expected: /ssss/-/p/-/iiii/
Touch-and-say using the second row.
In the second row, student touches first tile and says /s/, touches second tile and says /p/, touches third tile and says /i/.
Here's the tough part. Touch-and-say until you find the sounds that are different. SPA. SPI.
Expected: The last sounds are different.
Good listening. So go ahead and change the last tile in the new word ... to show that it's different.
Student changes the last tile in the second row.
That's perfect. Now go ahead and wash off those tiles.

Dictate the following pairs for comparison:
1. UD vs. UCH
2. KOV vs. TOV
3. BA vs. KA
4. UNT vs. UST
5. GRO vs. GRA

sections.title: Task D: Blend 2 and 3 Sounds into Real Words

steps.text: Now I'll give you some sounds. You'll blend them together to create a real word. Let me show you what I mean.
Tutor touches each tile while saying: 'This tile says /a/, this tile says /t/.' Now you touch-and-say those sounds.
Expected: Student touches first tile saying /a/, then second tile saying /t/.
Slowly blend them together.
Expected: /aaaaa/-/t/
Say it fast like a word.
Expected: AT
Perfect. Go ahead and wash off those tiles.

Dictate the following sound sequences for the student to blend into words:
1. /a/ /t/ (AT)
2. /h/ /a/ /v/ (HAVE)
3. /n/ /o/ /k/ (KNOCK)
4. /f/ /u/ /j/ (FUDGE)
5. /m/ /a/ /ch/ (MATCH)
6. /th/ /i/ /n/ (THIN)
7. /e/ /n/ /d/ (END)
8. /l/ /a/ /m/ (LAMB)
Now you're ready for the last step in this book - creating words that rhyme. First let me give you some sounds.
Here are the sounds: /s/ /a/ /d/. Touch-and-say, then tell me the word.
Expected: Student touches, blends, and says SAD.
Which tile would you change to create a word that rhymes?
Expected: The first one.
Right. So go ahead and create a word that rhymes with SAD.
Student replaces the first tile, says its sound, then says the rhyming word.
Create two more words that rhyme.
Expect words like BAD, DAD, FAD, HAD, MAD, PAD, TAD, etc. Once done, wash off tiles.
Assign these sounds to three tiles: /l/ /i/ /p/.
Have the student create rhyming words for LIP. Expect dip, hip, nip, sip, tip, whip, yip, zip, chip, ship.
